$comment: Declared CSV coverage, one entry per directory under backend/internal/domain/.
scripts/lib/csv-coverage.mjs reads this; verify.mjs fails when a domain is absent
from it, or when a declaration disagrees with the routes that domain registers.
States: yes | no | deferred. Anything that is not 'yes' needs a why.<capability>,
and a 'deferred' reason must start with the issue number tracking it.
The point is not to force every domain to have CSV. It is that a domain without
it has said so on purpose. Six domains went eight releases with no export and no
record of whether that was a decision, which is the gap this closes.

why.import: Contracts arrive one at a time from the KO. There has never been a batch to load, and the table has no unique index to dedupe an upload against.
why.template: No import, so a template would be a file that leads nowhere.

why.import: A channel row is meaningless without a plan and a net that already exist. A CSV would bypass every cross-domain check the editor performs.
why.template: No import, so a template would be a file that leads nowhere.

why.export: An append-only record of who did what. Handing it out as a file is a different decision from showing it in an admin view, and has not been taken.
why.import: Writing to the audit log from a file forges history.
why.template: No import, so nothing to template.

why.export: The roster plus role is PII. Not a download.
why.import: Users are synced from Entra on first sign-in. A CSV would create accounts the identity provider does not know about.
why.template: No import, so nothing to template.

why.export: A dozen rows, all visible in the sidebar dialog.
why.import: Sections are created a few at a time in a dialog, and deleting one has to prompt for terminal and kit reassignment. A bulk path would have to reimplement that.
why.template: No import, so nothing to template.
